title: Uniform excess contraction under random walks
statement:
Let $G$ be a regular multigraph of degree $D>0$ on a finite, nonempty vertex set $V$. Assume that $G$ is connected and not bipartite. Then there is a walk length $k$ such that, for every function $p:V\to\mathbb{Q}$ with $\sum_{v\in V}p(v)=1$, the distribution obtained by taking a uniformly random length-$k$ walk from a starting vertex sampled according to $p$ satisfies
\[\max_{v\in V}\left(\sum_{u\in V}p(u)\Pr[\text{the walk from }u\text{ ends at }v]-\frac{1}{|V|}\right)\leq \left(1-\frac{1}{|V|^{10|V|}}\right)\max_{v\in V}\left(p(v)-\frac{1}{|V|}\right).\]
hypotheses_covered: $G$ is a regular multigraph of degree $D>0$
The vertex set $V$ is finite and nonempty
